previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, chronic diastolic heart failure, diabetes with neuropathy and nephropathy, and a history of hemolytic anemia, was admitted for left lower extremity cellulitis. He presented with three days of increasing redness, warmth, and swelling without fever. He was started on IV vancomycin and Zosyn, with improvement in symptoms and inflammatory markers. Blood cultures were negative, DVT ultrasound was negative, and Lyme serology was non-reactive. He was transitioned to oral cephalexin for a 10-day course. His hemoglobin remained stable, and his kidney function improved to baseline. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in oncology and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo man with h/o multiple myeloma on 
carfilzomib for approximately ___ years, s/p 1 dose of revlimid, 
who presents with AMS, fall, and fever, now found to have 
Listeria bacteremia and meningitis.

# Listeria sepsis/meningitis: Patient presented with fever and 
AMS. He was treated broadly with vancomycin and cefepime. 
Admission blood cultures subsequently grew Listeria 
monocytogenes. ID was consulted and antibiotics were changed to 
ampicillin, gentamicin, and meropenem. Given AMS lumbar puncture 
was done, which revealed very marked pleiocytosis with 
neutrophilic predominance. Per ID recommendations he was 
continued on ampicillin (to be continued for 6 weeks) and 
gentamicin (to be continued for 2 weeks). He will follow up 
outpatient with infectious disease.

# Right precentral gyrus CVA: As part of workup for altered 
mental status, meningitis, concern for brain abscess, patient 
had MRI brain which revealed small acute infarct in right 
precentral gyrus. Neurology were consulted and he had MRA 
head/neck, which was normal, and echocardiogram, which did not 
identify acute thrombus and was similar to prior. Unclear if 
from cardioembolic event. Rapid mental status improvement with 
treatment of infection suggested that infarct was not related to 
his altered mental status. Antiplatelet/anticoagulation was 
initially held given thrombocytopenia, but ASA was resumed after 
platelet count improved. Home statin continued, plan to 
follow-up with outpatient neurologist on discharge. 

# Chronic diastolic heart failure: Home furosemide was initially 
held in setting of sepsis, altered mental status, and restarted 
prior to discharge. During course he required diuresis with IV 
Lasix boluses given hypervolemia in setting of high amounts of 
iVF with antibiotics. Home atenolol was adjusted for 
bradycardia, and spironolactone, statin were continued. Lasix 
was held on discharge. 

# Pancytopenia: Presented with pancytopenia thought in setting 
of bacteremia, chronic treatment with carfilzomib. He required 
1U plts and 3U pRBCs during his stay. H/H 7.7/24.3 on day of 
discharge. He does have history of chronic AIHA and home 7.5 mg 
prednisone was continued for this.

# Multiple myeloma: S/p 28 cycles of carfilzomib with increasing 
IgA paraproteinemia. He had received a single dose of revlimid 
as outpatient prior to admission. Revlimid was held here. He was 
continued on prophylaxis with allopurinol, atovaquone, and 
acyclovir. He will follow up with his outpatient oncologist for 
further treatment plans.

# Type 2 diabetes: Insulin dependent. Per last ___ notes was 
on lantus 60 U qAM, glipizide XR 5 mg bid. Last A1c below goal 
at 5.6 in ___. Glipizide was held and lantus downtitrated 
for hypoglycemia in ___. Likely can consider decreasing lantus 
as outpatient given HgbA1c below goal and concern for 
hypoglycemia.

# Chronic kidney disease: Creatinine 2.1 on admission and 
downtrended prior to discharge. Medications were renally dosed.

# H/o atrial flutter s/p ablation: Patietn remained in regular 
rhythm with no thrombus identified on echocardiogram. Home 
atenolol was adjusted for bradycardia in ___.
